profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This is US Signal OR01 facility in Bend, Oregon, marketed on the company own site as a green data center emphasizing energy efficient operations. US Signal is a Grand Rapids, Michigan based provider of colocation, cloud, and managed IT infrastructure services, operating several colocation data centers across the Midwest and beyond, including an acquired facility in Aurora, Illinois reported in trade press. A data center listing aggregator lists the Bend facility capacity at approximately 0.9 megawatts, treated here as an unverified lead rather than a confirmed specification since it comes from a directory rather than US Signal own site. US Signal positions itself as a regional colocation and managed services provider serving customers who need secure data center space outside the largest coastal hubs. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
US Signal OR01 in Bend is listed in one aggregator at approximately 0.9 MW, but this figure is unverified against the operator's own published specifications. The facility sits outside the state's eight data centers with published capacity figures and ranks ninth among all mapped sites in Oregon by the aggregator's estimate. At the aggregator's stated 0.9 MW, assuming 40 kW per rack as a common colocation density, the site would hold roughly 22 racks, an estimate with no confirmation from the operator.

Oregon has published capacity totaling 156.6 MW across eight confirmed facilities and 133 mapped locations overall. US Signal OR01's unverified 0.9 MW would represent less than 1 percent of the state's published capacity if confirmed.

This campus does not appear in US Signal's own publicly available specifications and cannot be assessed for AI relevance without verified power availability, cooling capacity, or grid connectivity data from the operator. The aggregator figure is a lead only, not a fact about what the facility actually supplies.
